articles.author: Sora2 Hub Team
articles.description:
Most weak image-to-video clips fail for the same reason: the prompt describes the picture again instead of describing the movement. The model can already see your image. What it needs from you is how the camera moves, what moves inside the frame, and what must stay still.
This cheat sheet collects the camera moves that work reliably, the wording that tends to produce them, and the mistakes that cause warping and drift.
A good image-to-video prompt usually answers three questions, in this order:
Camera: How does the camera move? (push in, orbit, pan, static)
Subject: What moves in the scene? (hair in the wind, steam rising, a person turning their head)
Constraints: What must not change? (the logo, the face, the product shape, the background)
Example:
Slow push-in toward the cup. Steam rises…
articles.title: Camera Motion Prompts for AI Image-to-Video: A Practical Cheat Sheet

articles.author: Affix Center Softech Services Pvt. Ltd
articles.description:
A penetration test is only useful if developers can act on the result. A long PDF of scanner output does not help anyone ship a fix. Here is what a development team should expect from a vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT), based on how the security team at Affix Center in Mumbai runs these engagements.
Infrastructure, applications and APIs, not only the public website
Secure configuration reviews of the systems the app runs on
Controlled penetration testing, so production is not put at risk
A risk-ranked report, so the team knows what to fix first
Remediation steps for each finding
Both an executive report and a technical report, because managers and developers need different detail
A retest after the fixes, to confirm they worked
A secure development lifecycle
Authentication and authorisation on every API
Encryption at rest and in transit
Role-based access, with audit and compliance traceability
Run VAPT at least once a year, and again after any major change to an application or to infrastructure.
If your organisation faces NIC or CERT-In empanelled security audits, plan time to fix the observations those audits raise. That work usually lands on the development team.
More detail on scope and process: Cyber Security and VAPT services by Affix Center
Written by the team at Affix Center, an IT services company in Lower Parel, Mumbai.
articles.title: What a VAPT report should hand back to your dev team

articles.description:
The worst failure mode a data API can have is not an error. It's a 200 with an empty body. Nothing is red, nothing retries, nothing pages anyone — the caller just concludes there was no data, and moves on with a wrong answer.
Over four days of edge-case testing on our own Actors we found four separate bugs with exactly that shape, and all four came down to a character the user couldn't see. None of them were exotic. Every one of them is the kind of thing that survives a code review, because the code reads correctly right up until you look at the bytes.
Here they are, in the order we found them, with what we actually measured.
The commonest text-field artifact in the world is a leading or trailing space — double-click a word in a spreadsheet, drag-select a phrase from a PDF, paste from a ch…

Advisory documents get read in one pass: an investor memo, a due-diligence answer, a client strategy PDF. Nobody skims them twice. That makes them word-dense — every sentence is doing paid work, and small wording changes move decisions.

Dropped hedges. "We believe the sector faces challenges" → "the sector faces challenges." Removing "we believe" is a conviction upgrade. Automated diffs flag exactly these: we believe, we think, in our view, expected, likely.
